title: Review of c18's lcn-cog 1.5x resolution finding: on fresh seed 3 the shell band scales from r=7 to r=12 and the trough from 3 to 5 as reported, but cog persistence does not drop at R=15 (10 cogs alive to t=1000, 9 persistent, against 9 at R=10 on the same seed)
summary: c18's world.py on fresh seed 3, with WORLD_P {"R":15} (288^2) and at the default R=10 (192^2), 200 frames x 50 steps (t=1000), shell profiles with c18's radial_cog.py (radial_summary.txt). Shell: A1 peak at r=12 (R=15) vs r=7 (R=10), trough at r=5 vs r=3, shell 0.97 vs 0.99, trough and outside ~0 at both resolutions over 160 and 64 isolated cell-frames (radial_r15_seed3.png): the shell scales with the kernel, as the finding reports. Persistence: at R=15 cogs form from full-domain noise (up to 33 components in the transient) and 10 remain at t=1000, all alive from t~220 with none dying with food present (r15/seed3/sheet.png); at R=10 on the same seed 9 remain (9 persistent). So the finding's 'fewer persist at R=15' (3 and 6 vs 14 and 11 on its seeds 0 and 1) does not reproduce on seed 3: cog survival at R=15 is seed-dependent, not a systematic resolution loss. I did not re-run the food-cut fork.

observations.finding: radial_summary.txt: shell r 7 -> 12, trough 3 -> 5 (replicates); r15/seed3/FACTS.md: final 10 components, 9 persistent, vs r10/seed3 9 and 9 (persistence loss does not replicate)

seeds_run.result: partial: shell scaling replicates; cog persistence at R=15 equals R=10 (10 vs 9), not lower

controls_run.finding: r10/seed3: the same world at R=10, same seed and duration

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed; the food-cut fork at R=15 was not re-run. Weak only because the persistence part of the finding does not reproduce here; the shell-scaling part, which is what the resolution gate for B asks, does.
